## Conditional statements

Python evaluates a condition to determine whether an indented block should be
executed.

::: {.callout-tip .teaching-tip title="Teaching tip"}
Ask students to predict the output before executing the Python statement. Compare
their predictions afterward.
:::

:::: {.callout-note .ask-students title="Ask students"}
What happens when `destination == "JFK"` evaluates to `False`?

```python
destination = "LHR"

if destination == "JFK":
    print("Flight to New York")
else:
    print("Different destination")
```

::: {.callout-explanation}
**Follow-up:** Ask students which branch runs, and why the comparison is
false.
:::
::::

:::: {.callout-important .common-misconception title="Common misconception"}
Indentation defines which statements belong to a block. It is not merely visual
formatting.

```python
if destination == "JFK":
    print("New York")
    print("International flight")

print("Check completed")
```

::: {.callout-explanation}
The last statement runs independently of the condition because it is not
indented.
:::
::::

::: {.callout-caution .timing-transition title="Timing / transition"}
5 minutes. Connect this example to the preceding discussion of Boolean
expressions.
:::

::: {.callout-note .instructor-hint title="Instructor hint"}
Before class, confirm that the working directory is set to the folder containing
the files used in the live demonstration.
:::
